analysis.title: Macro2Markets US Monthly Outlook: Rates Maelstrom Amid Manufacturing Momentum?
key_insights: AI has produced a concentrated investment boom: about $400bn of real investment in tech sits above the pre-AI trend, driven mostly by computer equipment, where annual growth approached 80%. Broader demand growth still resembles the shallow post-GFC expansion.

Real final sales to private domestic purchasers are growing at roughly the 2.5-3.5% pace of the post-GFC expansion. MUFG calls this moderate at best and stays cautious on growth until activity broadens.
The hiring rate has fallen to its lowest level since 2011 and the job finding rate sits at 2015 levels. JOLTS layoffs remain below the pre-pandemic trend but are rising in white-collar industries.

Advanced manufacturing is a bright spot. Profit per dollar of sales has risen sharply in AI-adjacent subsectors (machinery, computers and electronics), and job openings, the NFP manufacturing diffusion index and ISM Manufacturing PMI have turned higher.
The 3-month annualized change in core PCE has reached 2%. If the recent soft monthly pace holds, it stays near 2% through year-end, reducing the need for multiple rate hikes.

Price growth is broad despite soft core PCE. The share of expenditures growing above 3% annualized and the fraction of PCE items with rising prices both signal more inflation persistence than core PCE suggests. Chair Warsh references the distribution of PCE price growth.

Fed funds futures price about three more hikes by September 2027, slightly fewer than last month. MUFG's base case is no change in the policy rate, with at most one hike in Dec 2026 and a cut in Sep 2027, and sees the market path as aggressive.
The September SEP was more hawkish: the median dot shows an additional hike versus June, and the median unemployment projection fell to 4.1%. MUFG says the SEP looks influenced by recency bias.

The FOMC's diffusion index on unemployment risks turned negative for the first time since 2021 and growth risks flipped to the upside. With the natural rate of unemployment estimated at about 4.3-4.4%, MUFG thinks the FOMC is overestimating labor market health.

The UST sell-off came in three waves: energy prices in 1H26, the hawkish pivot by new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh over the summer, and a September reprice in which long bonds had one of their worst months in years. Drivers were negative global rates and IG credit supply, including from hyperscalers.
MUFG raised its rates forecast by 25-50bps in all quarters through the forecast horizon, but warns the market may have overshot after pricing in much of the Fed path.

Recent strong UST auctions suggest the backup brought enough concession to attract value investors. MUFG says long-term rates may be rounding out a near-term local high and calls Treasuries deep value, while noting top-ticking is ill-advised.
Long-dated forwards (10y10y) have moved far more than 1y1y since the 2022-23 hiking cycle, so fiscal and supply concerns are showing up in long forwards and term premia, not Fed policy alone.
Rate volatility has more two-way risk after a late September/early October blow-off in long-term yields, with the range of MOVE outcomes widening at higher rate levels.

Most of the rise in 10-year yields reflects real rates and repricing of Fed expectations (risk-neutral rate) rather than term premium, though fiscal fears keep yields up. Tariffs, debt-financed tax cuts and the war are inflationary.

Since the pandemic USTs have been a weaker equity hedge: bonds rallied 9% and 5% in the last two equity drawdowns (equities down 13% and 25%), versus 10-40% rallies before 2020. MUFG still expects USTs to hedge a risk-off move, with long-term rates able to fall 100bps or more if risk-off lasts over a month.

The US midterms are a bond catalyst. A Democratic win could mean fiscal gridlock and more AI regulation in 2027, supporting USTs. A Republican win enabling continued fiscal expansion would be harder on bonds.
Interest costs are projected at over twice the primary deficit by 2032, keeping the deficit near 6% of GDP. Lowering debt to GDP needs nominal growth of 5% or more with rates 200-300bps lower.

Net interest expense exceeded defense spending in 2025 (Ferguson's law). Forward 10-year rates are shown near an unsustainably high 6% by 2032, which MUFG says is inconsistent with moderate growth and 2% inflation.

About $535bn of USTs carry coupons above 5%, under 2% of the total. If the curve stays near or above 5%, Treasury will restack higher coupons into the debt stack, embedding higher servicing costs for years.

Treasury's reliance on T-bills (about 23% of debt) makes funding costs more pro-cyclical and less predictable. Bessent has continued the predecessor's bill-heavy policy, and MUFG expects tweaks rather than wholesale changes to debt funding.
Foreign holders (32% of $29.0T) and the Fed (14%) have slowed UST purchases. Private demand from ETFs (2-year CAGR 24.2%), GSEs (27.0%) and nonfinancial businesses (20.6%) has grown fastest.

The US is projected to hit the debt limit in early FY27 and exhaust extraordinary measures by mid 2027. A Democratic sweep or split Congress raises the risk of delay, and a Treasury buyback program and central clearing of repo in mid 2027 may add collateral demand.
MUFG forecasts the Fed funds rate at 4.125% through Q2-2027 and 3.875% in Q3-2027, with the 10-year at 4.75% in Q4-2026 falling to 4.375% in Q3-2027. The 10-year last traded at 5.24%.
MUFG's 12-18 month scenario probabilities as of Oct 9, 2026: stagflation 35%, stagnation 25%, mild/hard recession 25%, goldilocks 10%, boom 5%.

sector_views.rationale: Treasuries are in deep-value territory after the sell-off and a constructive setup for high-quality fixed income (USTs and MBS) may emerge over 6-12 months if markets stabilize through the midterms.
Profit per dollar of sales and labor demand are rising in AI-adjacent subsectors, making it a bright spot in a stagnant labor market.

trade_ideas.description: Long US Treasuries and MBS (high-quality fixed income) on a 6-12 month view if markets stabilize through the midterms
trade_ideas.rationale: Treasuries are in deep-value territory and yields offer income and total return potential as a portfolio hedge.
trade_ideas.risk: A Republican win enabling continued fiscal expansion would be more challenging for bonds.

risk_factors: Hawkish Fed repricing could overshoot or the FOMC could be wrong about labor market strength.
Fiscal and supply concerns keep term premia and long-dated forwards elevated.
Heavy IG credit supply, including from hyperscalers, competes with Treasuries for capital.
Debt ceiling delay after the midterms, with extraordinary measures exhausted by mid 2027.
Rising interest costs, forecast at over twice the primary deficit by 2032.
Concentrated AI investment without broadening growth, and falling hiring with rising white-collar layoffs.
Equity correction risk, with USTs a weaker hedge than before 2020.
Pro-cyclical Treasury funding from heavy T-bill reliance.
charts_described: Real fixed investment chart: computer equipment growth near 80% YoY versus software growth in line with pre-pandemic levels.
Fed funds futures chart: about 3 hikes priced by September 2027 versus MUFG's forecast.
Debt-to-GDP heatmap: marketable UST debt to GDP by 2030 under growth and rate scenarios, with a 2.5% average primary deficit assumed.
vol_and_positioning: The MOVE index spiked in late September/early October after a blow-off in long-term rates, and MUFG sees more two-way risk in rate vol at higher yield levels.
Short spurts in implied vol such as the one-week Liberation Day spike tend to fade quickly.
Stocks are described as ripe for a correction and stretched versus long bonds on a 30Y yield minus S&P dividend yield basis.
Recent strong UST auctions point to value-investor demand after the backup.
Private UST demand, notably ETFs, has jumped, and foreign demand has shifted from central banks to private buyers, likely hedge funds via the basis trade.
geopolitical: Energy price moves and the war are cited as inflationary and drove the first wave of the UST sell-off in 1H26.
Supply shocks could fade if the war ends, which MUFG cites as a reason the market's hawkish Fed path may be too aggressive.
US midterm elections: a Democratic win could bring fiscal gridlock and more AI regulation, while a Republican win could extend fiscal expansion.
Euro-area concerns could lift the USD and trigger a risk-off move in which USTs act as a hedge.
Tariffs under Trump 2.0 fiscal policy are cited as inflationary.

tension_points.bull_case: Futures price about three more hikes by September 2027 and the SEP turned hawkish on inflation fears, with unemployment projected at 4.1%.
tension_points.bear_case: MUFG sees the base case as flat policy with at most one Dec 2026 hike and a cut in Sep 2027, citing recency bias in the SEP, a weaker labor market than the FOMC assumes, and possible fading supply shocks after the midterms.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Republican win enabling continued fiscal expansion, or inflation breadth staying high, would keep the hawkish path in play.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong auctions show value-investor demand, yields are historically high, and USTs are in deep-value territory.
tension_points.bear_case: Fiscal supply, heavy IG issuance and term premium keep pressure on long-term rates, and USTs have hedged equity drawdowns less since the pandemic.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Republican win enabling continued fiscal expansion would be more challenging for bonds.
